title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented Penn traditions spanning first-year welcome, class milestones, campus ritual, and athletic spirit.

cards.title: Toss toast at Franklin Field
cards.subtitle: Penn football tradition
cards.notes: At home football games, listen for “Here’s a toast to dear old Penn,” then observe the coordinated bread toss from the stands.
cards.short_summary: A football-game ritual tied to Penn’s unofficial alma mater.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn’s Office of Student Affairs documents toast throwing after the third quarter of football games, timed to the lyric “Here’s a toast to dear old Penn.”
cards.source_title: Campus Traditions | Office of Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Occurs at Penn home football games; follow current stadium guidance and event policies.

cards.title: Mark junior-to-senior year on Hey Day
cards.subtitle: Annual class-rank celebration
cards.notes: Watch for the third-year class’s red shirts, mock skimmer hats, and canes as Penn marks its move to fourth-year status.
cards.short_summary: Penn’s annual rising-senior ceremony, begun in 1916.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Today reports that Hey Day began in 1916 and uses hats, canes, and a class celebration to symbolize third-years’ rise to fourth-year rank.
cards.source_title: Class of 2027 sparks traditional spirit on Hey Day | Penn Today
cards.access_notes: For Penn third-year students; date and program are announced annually.

cards.title: Find a graduating class’s Ivy Stone
cards.subtitle: Campus-wide class memorial tradition
cards.notes: Look closely at College Hall, Penn Commons, and other campus locations for engraved stones that record graduating classes and Ivy Day.
cards.short_summary: Each graduating class leaves a physical campus marker.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn states that each graduating class has contributed an Ivy Stone to campus since 1873.
cards.source_title: Ivy Stones 1873–2025 | Office of Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Stones are installed around campus; view them from publicly accessible outdoor areas.

cards.title: See the Ivy Day Ceremony
cards.subtitle: Graduating fourth-year recognition
cards.notes: Follow the annual Ivy Day coverage to see the graduating class unveil its Ivy Stone and recognize student leadership and service.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Today says the annual Ivy Day celebration includes unveiling a class Ivy Stone and an awards ceremony for graduating fourth-year students.
cards.source_title: Class of 2026 Ivy Day Ceremony | Penn Today
cards.access_notes: Held during Alumni Weekend; current ceremony details are announced by Penn.

cards.title: Recognize the Spoon, Bowl, Cane, and Spade
cards.subtitle: Ivy Day’s historic class honors
cards.notes: At Ivy Day, notice the named Senior Honor Awards—Spoon, Bowl, Cane, and Spade—which link today’s recipients to Penn history.
cards.short_summary: Historic awards remain part of the Ivy Day tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Today identifies the Bowl, Spade, Cane, and Spoon as Senior Honor Awards presented at the Ivy Day Ceremony.
cards.source_title: Class of 2026 Ivy Day Ceremony | Penn Today
cards.access_notes: Recipients and ceremony details vary by graduating class.

cards.title: Raise a lantern at U-Night
cards.subtitle: Second-year class milestone
cards.notes: Second-year students gather near sunset and join the lantern exercise that marks their transition toward junior year at Penn.
cards.short_summary: A newer class tradition centered on light and the halfway point.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Today reports that each second-year class has gathered since 2019 for U-Night, including a traditional lantern exercise.
cards.source_title: Penn’s Class of 2027 marks the midway at U-Night | Penn Today
cards.access_notes: For Penn second-year students; location and timing are announced annually.

cards.title: Hear the Econ Scream
cards.subtitle: Lower Quadrangle, before Microeconomics 001 midterm
cards.notes: If you are nearby at midnight before the first Microeconomics 001 midterm, expect the annual collective shout from the Junior Balcony.
cards.short_summary: A midnight stress-release ritual associated with Econ 001.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn’s Office of Student Affairs documents Econ Scream as a collective midnight shout on the Junior Balcony before the first Microeconomics 001 midterm.
cards.source_title: Campus Traditions | Office of Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Timing follows the first Microeconomics 001 midterm; be considerate of nearby residents and campus rules.

cards.title: Track Penn’s Spring Fling
cards.subtitle: Annual spring campus tradition
cards.notes: Check Penn’s current program for Spring Fling activities, a campus tradition that began in 1973 and has often used the Quadrangle.
cards.short_summary: A long-running springtime Penn event with Quad roots.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn’s Office of Student Affairs states that students began the annual Spring Fling tradition in 1973 and that it has taken place in the Quadrangle in many years.
cards.source_title: Campus Traditions | Office of Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Programming, access, and location vary by year; consult current Penn announcements.

cards.title: Enter Penn at Convocation
cards.subtitle: Franklin Field welcome ceremony
cards.notes: Incoming students process into Penn’s formal welcome ceremony, the opening milestone in a sequence that later includes Hey Day and Commencement.
cards.short_summary: A first-year ceremony with roots in Penn’s nineteenth century.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn’s Office of the University Secretary describes Convocation as Penn’s formal incoming-class welcome and dates its modern form to around 1894.
cards.source_title: Convocation | Office of the University Secretary
cards.access_notes: For the incoming class; Penn announces the current ceremony’s date and attendance information.

cards.title: Send off seniors at Final Toast
cards.subtitle: Hey Day’s senior-class counterpart
cards.notes: During Hey Day, the outgoing senior class gathers for its separate sendoff while the junior class is inaugurated into its final undergraduate year.
cards.short_summary: A senior-to-alumni milestone held alongside Hey Day.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Today reports that Final Toast, first celebrated in 2009, celebrates the senior class and symbolically elevates participants to alumni status.
cards.access_notes: Held in connection with Hey Day; participation details are announced through Penn Traditions.
